newsitem.title: USA: BEFORE THE BELL - Novellus off sharply.
newsitem.headline: BEFORE THE BELL - Novellus off sharply.

text.p: Novellus Systems Inc stock fell to 61-1/2 from 75-1/4 before the U.S. market open Monday in a selloff triggered by news of possible financial damage to the company from a patent infringement lawsuit, traders said.
Novellus also announced a decline in first quarter net income to $0.91 per share from $1.55, and quarterly revenues that fell to $101.6 million from $115.3 million.
While the per-share net was $0.01 above the Zack's Investment Research consensus estimate, traders said selling was further spurred by a first quarter book-to-bill ratio that fell below one-to-one.
"The book-to-bill below one and the legal news is bad for Novellus," said a trader.
In addition to announcing quarterly earnings this morning, Novellus said it will seek to overturn a patent infringement lawsuit versus Applied Materials Inc.
But Novellus said that if its defenses were not upheld, damages assessed against it could have a material adverse impact on the company's financial condition.
As for the book-to-bill, a ratio of one-to-one means that for every $100 of equipment shipped, $100 of new orders were booked. It is considered an important indicator of sales trends.
Also, a PaineWebber source said the firm lowered its rating on the stock to neutral from attractive,
Applied Material shares fell to 48-5/8 from 50-1/4.
Elsewhere, Intel Corp shares climbed one to 131-1/2, a move traders said was a bounce off the stock's 6-3/4 point decline Friday.
Intel is expected to announce quarterly results after today's market close.
